title: Mitchell Starc Dethrones Jasprit Bumrah as World’s Top-Ranked Test Bowler
excerpt: The Australian left-arm pacer’s 10-wicket haul against Bangladesh propels him to No. 1 for the first time, ending Bumrah’s reign of nearly 700 days.
body:
• Mitchell Starc climbed two places to reach No. 1 in the ICC Test bowling rankings with 872 rating points, surpassing Bumrah (862) and Matt Henry (861)
  • Starc’s 10-wicket match haul (6/12 and 4/39) in the second Test against Bangladesh in Mackay earned him Player of the Match and Player of the Series awards
  • Bumrah’s absence from India’s ongoing Test series against Sri Lanka due to a left-knee injury contributed to the change at the top

Australia’s Mitchell Starc has reached the summit of the ICC Test bowling rankings for the first time in his 15-year career, dethroning India’s Jasprit Bumrah in the latest update released on Wednesday.

The 36-year-old left-arm fast bowler produced a devastating 10-wicket match haul — figures of 6/12 and 4/39 — in the second Test against Bangladesh at Mackay, bowling Australia to an innings-and-51-run victory that levelled the two-match series 1-1.

How the Rankings Shifted

Starc jumped two places to the top with 872 rating points, leapfrogging both Bumrah (862) and New Zealand’s Matt Henry (861). His previous career-best ranking was second, which he first achieved after the Boxing Day Ashes Test last December.

Bumrah had first reached the No. 1 position in February 2024 and held it for much of the past two-plus years, accumulating a combined 697 days at the top — the most by any Indian bowler in history and the 14th-most ever. His latest stint ended primarily because a left-knee injury sustained during an ODI series against England in July ruled him out of India’s ongoing World Test Championship series against Sri Lanka.

Australian Dominance in Updated Rankings

Australia now boasts two bowlers in the top four. Captain Pat Cummins climbed one spot to fourth after taking six wickets in the Mackay Test, while veteran spinner Nathan Lyon rose two places to 10th.

England bowlers also made significant gains following their innings-and-103-run victory over Pakistan in Leeds. Ollie Robinson leapt 15 places to 11th after figures of 5/51 and 3/39, while Josh Tongue climbed 16 spots to 17th with eight wickets in the match.

India’s Movers in the Batting Charts

Rishabh Pant was the biggest mover among batters, climbing six places to share seventh with captain Shubman Gill after his quickfire half-century in India’s first-Test victory over Sri Lanka in Galle. India’s left-arm spinner Manav Suthar also gained 28 places to a career-best 48th among bowlers after his 10-wicket haul at Galle.

The top of the batting table remains unchanged, with England’s Harry Brook and Joe Root in first and second, followed by Australia’s Steve Smith and Travis Head.

Starc’s rise underscores his remarkable longevity. He has spent much of his career in the top 10 and continues to lead the wicket-taking charts in the current World Test Championship cycle, even as he turns 37 in January.
